title: Window 5b (Agent 8, run-2 task #7 follow-up): TimerQueue wait modes on devoff4 (S4a), all with the 8 timer cvars. d11 (spin wait) vs d11t (blocking wait, REX_TIMER_WAIT_BLOCKING=1) vs d11p (precise wait, timer_queue_precise_wait=true)
notes: Follow-up window proposed by Agent 8 (run-2 task #7) on 2026-11-22 for the 01:00-06:45 slot; Agent 1 picks. Staged and checked with build/agent8/w-followup/stage-window.ps1. GO (a): 'GO W5b matrix-window5b.json <sha256> only=d11,d11t,d11p repeats=6': one unscored cold run (devoff4), then 6 round-robin rounds rotated each round (two full 3x3 Latin squares: each arm in each position twice): 1 + 18 = 19 runs. GO (b), the same file and sha256: 'only=d11,d11t repeats=6': 1 + 12 = 13 runs (the blocking wait alone).

Question: do the new TimerQueue waits cost tail while they save CPU? W5 (build/agent8/matrix/20261122-1756; read-out build/agent8/readout/w5/READOUT.md) left one lead: d11t vs d11 (same bin and cvars, only the wait differs) p99 +8.2 % (T-std [+0.5, +16.6]*, B-block [+1.6, +15.3]*) and 1 % low -7.7 % (B-block [-13.8, -1.2]*); T-heavy 1 % low vs base: d11t -8.5 % [-14.4, -2.3]* and d11p -11.0 % [-16.7, -4.8]*. Without run 1821-d11t-r3 no CI excludes 0. Game CPU vs base: d11t -13.7 % and d11p -12.2 % (better). 6 rounds give 6 per-round differences per pair.
All three arms ran in W5 (16/16 runs OK; Agent 6's logdiff: only the expected timer lines). The shared cold run is on devoff4, the bin of every arm, so every scored run is a warm run of one bin.

Proof per run, checked before any fps is read (as W5's R7): every game.log shows 'Host timer resolution set to 1 ms (background opt-out on)'. Every d11p game.log has exactly one 'TimerQueue: precise wait (timer_queue_precise_wait)'; d11 and d11t have none. d11t logs nothing for the blocking wait: its proof is REX_TIMER_WAIT_BLOCKING in run.json env_set, which d11 and d11p must not have. TimerQueue CPU (threads.csv, % of one core): d11 > 20 % (spin); d11t and d11p < 15 % (the read-out gate; W5 measured 4-6 %). Then Agent 11's 3-mode slow-state check (bench/agent11/timerq_slowstate_3mode.ps1) on every run.

REX_TIMER_WAIT_BLOCKING is presence-only: =0 or an empty value still turns the blocking wait on, and with both set the precise wait wins (Agent 11). The runner sets it for d11t runs only and restores the environment after every run; the launcher removes every allowed key from its own environment before each window.

Window: 5 s settle + 55 s warm-up from the first frame, then 50 s measured, so every window starts >= 60 s after the first frame (min_window_after_ff_s 60, Agent 1's floor); the runner flags window_before_floor (excluded) below 59.5 s. The cold run: 55 s warm-up, 30 s window.

One frame source for every arm: perf.csv (frames perf), uncapped (framerate_limit=0), the same driver (drivers/thread-cpu.ps1 -> threads.csv). Runner flags on every run: --audio_mute=true --pause_when_unfocused=false --native_settings_load=false --discord_rpc=false.

sys_csv: drivers/sys-csv.ps1 logs the system state every 1 s (sys.csv, sys.json). Input during the window, the game losing the foreground, battery, battery saver, a power-plan change, a non-default input desktop or a screensaver exclude a run from summary.md (it stays in results.csv, under 'Flagged runs'). Light phase: a game.log with < 30 'FAILED: path=d:\INSTALL*.DAT' lines (normal boot: 34) is excluded (light_phase).

Read-out: Agent 8's W5 procedure (perf-notes/agent8-window3.md L920-1058 and its addendum; build/agent8/scratch/w5-readout.ps1) with d11 as the reference: T-std for median ms and fps, B-block for p99 and the 1 % low, timerq3, the slow-state scan and the sys.csv audit. A timing claim needs a CI that excludes 0; otherwise the row reads 'overlap' (no measurable difference).

Environment: like W4b and W5, after the 08:29 Windows Update. If the power overlay is not W5's best_efficiency, compare W5b only within itself and quote W5 only as a lead. Timing comes only from the user's unlocked desktop (Agent 5's overnight launcher); agent runs of this matrix (-Quick, hidden desktop) are functional only.
